source.check: Returning Officer's Notice of Result: the name is entered in column 5 for this division, no poll having been taken

note: Triennial election of the twenty-eight rural district divisions, poll 2 June 1955. No division was contested: twenty-eight members were returned unopposed on the nomination of 17 May, the Unionists gaining two seats where the Nationalists made no nomination (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8). The full return is taken from the Returning Officer's 'Notice of Result of Elections' for the Rural District of Strabane, 1955, signed by W. S. Moody and printed in the Strabane Chronicle of 28 May 1955, p. 2, which lists every division and the member elected in column 5, no poll having been taken. Party labels are not printed in the notice and none is recorded. The notice prints 'Dooratt' for Doorat; the dataset spelling is used. Three pairings are corroborated by later rounds: Glenmornan (James McCormick, who contests the division in 1961), Douglas (David Beattie, who contests Douglas Bridge in 1949), and Sion (E. T. R. Herdman, who contests it in 1952). Returned unopposed.
